html:
The Mongol-speaking herders of the Mongolian plateau, shown here in 1100, a century before Genghis Khan united them. Their map shape stretches from the Altai to the forests of the Amur.

In 1100 there was no Mongol state. The plateau was shared by rival Mongol and Turkic tribes: the Mongols proper near the Onon and Kherlen rivers, the Tatars to the east, the Kereits, Naimans and Merkits to the west and north. They lived from horses, sheep and cattle, moving between summer and winter pastures, and traded or raided along the frontier of the Khitan Liao dynasty, which claimed a loose overlordship.

In the 12th century a first Mongol league, the Khamag Mongol, rose and broke apart. Temüjin, born around 1162, rebuilt it by war and alliance, and in 1206 he was proclaimed Genghis Khan. From that union came the Mongol Empire.
